crm_notes: Encryption posture is primary purchase driver — they repeatedly asked: 'Who holds keys? Can we rotate without Redwood touching plaintext?'
In-transit: customer requires mutual TLS (mTLS) for all control-plane <-> dataplane traffic and for any inter-service RPCs. Prefer TLS1.3; support for strong cipher suites required.
mTLS details: will require Redwood-provided cert bundle for dataplane and customer trust anchor; customer will run their own cert authority in their VPC.
At-rest: customer insists on CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via AWS KMS (prefer CloudHSM-backed CMKs). Must demonstrate envelope encryption flow and HSM-backed root.

Key rotation: customer wants automated rotation policy with ability to perform emergency rotation. Must support manual rotate via customer's KMS, seamless re-wrapping of token stores, zero-downtime rotation guidance.

Secrets management: customer uses HashiCorp Vault (transit & kv). They want Redwood dataplane to retrieve runtime secrets from Vault using short-lived credentials; no long-lived plaintext secrets stored in Redwood control plane.

Audit logging: full request + response metadata (no PII content) to be forwarded to customer's SIEM in EU region. Retention policy: 7 years for auth/audit logs, configurable retention for payloads. Logs must include key IDs used for encryption operations.

Data residency: primary requirement is EU residency for training/embeddings storage. They will provision VPCs in eu-west-1; need confirmation that KMS CMKs are region-scoped and that Redwood control plane will not exfiltrate EU data.

Network/egress: customer will block outbound egress from private subnets; encrypted KMS calls must be possible via VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink). Customer expects a deployment option that uses VPC endpoints for KMS, ECR, S3, and telemetry sinks.
Compliance/attestations: customer requested SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence and an architecture diagram showing HSM, KMS boundaries and where audit logs are forwarded.
Quote from security lead: 'We need assurance that only our keys can decrypt model caches and embeddings — Redwood must provide clear BYOK flow and a proof-of-concept.'
POC ask: small-scale Private deployment in customer VPC, KMS CMK bound to model cache encryption, audit logs to customer's Splunk instance. 3-week POC timeline requested.

Notes on tradeoffs: customer prefers zero key custody by Redwood, but would allow Redwood-managed wrapping keys if legal language around key handling is explicit and meets policy. Legal prefers explicit SLAs for key destruction and rotation events.
Action items for AE/SE: prepare KMS integration runbook, draft BYOK contractual language for legal, confirm mTLS cert exchange flow and provide sample terraform for VPC endpoints.
Risks: need engineering signoff on supporting HSM-backed Cross-Region key access patterns; potential additional dev work to plug Vault auth method into dataplane startup sequence.
